readme.text:
[English](./README.md) | [简体中文](./README.zh.md)

ChatGPT Plus/Pro (Codex) adapter for the
[DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) LLM seam.

Routes a `codex` provider to `https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses`
using your **ChatGPT Plus/Pro subscription** — not an OpenAI API key, and not
the Codex desktop app. The OAuth flow, account/region headers, and request
translation mirror OpenCode's `plugins/openai/codex.ts`, so the same ChatGPT
account and the same public client are used.

| Model picker (ChatGPT Codex group) | `/codex-status` output |
|---|---|
|  |  |

The mockups above are illustrative — the real GUI gives you the same model
group and the same status text.

The plugin ships a `dsh.bundle` manifest, so the CLI installs it as a
profile layer and mounts the `codex` provider automatically — no manual
edit of `cordis.patch.yml` needed.

```bash

dsh plugin --profile web add file:/path/to/dsh-llm-codex
```

Restart the profile (or the web host) to apply the new bundle layer:

```bash

readme.section: in the terminal that runs the web host
readme.text:
Ctrl-C
dsh web
```

> `#last` is **not** a valid git ref. Use a branch name, commit SHA, or
> release tag instead.

The plugin's peer dependencies (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm`, `dsh-credentials`,
`dsh-settings`, `dsh-launch-environment`, `@deepseek-ai/schemastery`) come
from the DSH installation; on npm they are tagged `next (>=0.1.0-rc.8)`, so
add `--tag next` to your install command if pulling peer deps from npm.

In the GUI input:

```
/codex-login
```

- **browser** (default) — opens `auth.openai.com` OAuth in your browser and
  captures the redirect on `http://localhost:1455/auth/callback`.
- **headless** — prints a URL + code to enter at
  `auth.openai.com/codex/device` (no browser needed).

After authorization, verify with `/codex-status`, then pick any model in
the **ChatGPT Codex** group from the model selector:

| id | note |
|---|---|
| `gpt-5.6-sol` | Flagship Codex model (Sol), 400k context |
| `gpt-5.6-terra` | High-throughput Codex model (Terra) |
| `gpt-5.5` | Flagship Codex model, 400k context |
| `gpt-5.4` | General Codex model |
| `gpt-5.4-mini` | Lightweight / quick |
| `gpt-5.3-codex-spark` | Low-latency |

Use `/codex-logout` to clear credentials.

In `~/.dsh/settings.yaml`, under the `llm-codex:` section (hot-reloaded):

```yaml
llmcodex:   #   # callbackPort: 1455          # OAuth callback port (auto-b-fes if taken)
  # issuer: https://auth.openai.com
  # codexApiEndpoint: https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses
  # tokenRef: CHATGPT_OAUTH_TOKEN

The shipped catalog is advisory; you can append or replace it under
`llm-codex:`. Later entries with a duplicate id are dropped, so settings
can override a shipped entry by id without deleting it.

```yaml
llm-codex:
  extraModels:
    - id: gpt-5.6
      name: GPT-5.6 (Codex)

> The catalog is **advisory** — selectable does not mean callable. The Codex
> backend enforces which models your ChatGPT account can actually use
> (e.g. `gpt-5.6` is rejected with "not supported when using Codex with a
> ChatGPT account", so the shipped whitelist excludes it).

Environment variables `CODEX_API_ENDPOINT` / `CODEX_ISSUER` override the
endpoints; `CHATGPT_OAUTH_TOKEN` exported as a JSON bundle
`{"refresh":...,"access":...,"expires":...,"accountId":...}` is also
recognized as a credential source.

- `MISSING_CRED` → run `/codex-login`.
- `AUTH` (401/403) — usually a rotated refresh token (OpenCode or any other
  client sharing this account). Run `/codex-login` again. The error
  message in the GUI points to this case.
- HTTP 400 — check the `llm-codex` settings and model id.

readme.section: "I selected a codex model and everything broke"
readme.text:
The host's `session.selectModel` **persists every selection as the global
default model** (settings.yaml's `agent-default-model:` section). Once a
Codex model is picked, every new/resumed session defaults to the `codex`
route. If Codex then becomes unavailable (rotated token, exhausted quota,
backend rejection, stuck network), every session's messages fail — the
host looks entirely broken and survives a restart (the default is on
disk). **Don't delete `~/.dsh`.** To escape:

readme.section: "I selected a codex model and everything broke"
readme.text:
1. Open the model selector and switch back to DeepSeek (or any non-Codex
   model) — this rewrites the default automatically.
2. Or edit `~/.dsh/settings.yaml` and delete the whole `agent-default-model:`
   section.
3. Or run `/codex-logout` (clears credentials; combine with one of the
   above to clear the default).

`/codex-status` now also prints the warning when it detects this poisoned
default, so the cause is visible at a glance.

- **Billing** — uses your ChatGPT Plus/Pro subscription via OAuth. Separate
  from any OpenAI API key billing path. No API key required.
- **Shared account** — running the D plugin alongside OpenCode against the
  same ChatGPT account means each holds its own refresh token. Either side
  refreshing can rotate the other out; `/codex-login` restores it.
- **Proxy** — the adapter honors `http_proxy` / `https_proxy` / `no_proxy`
  via undici's `EnvHttpProxyAgent`. On networks where `auth.openai.com`
  rejects Node fetch's TLS profile (returns a bogus
  `unsupported_country_region_territory`), the OAuth/device endpoints
  automatically retry through the system `curl` binary, which honors the
  same proxy env vars.
- **Images** — declared image input; the adapter resolves the live
  attachment service from the harness so image-bearing messages serialize
  correctly. No-op when no attachments service is mounted.
- **Reasoning** — the Codex backend streams reasoning via summary events;
  `reasoning-delta` is emitted on a best-effort basis. `usage.reasoningTokens`
  is still reported. Replayed assistant turns drop reasoning content
  (the Responses API's input shape rejects `summary_text` c
